transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*looks up from organizing glass vials behind the counter, quill pausing mid-inventory*

Ah, Professor Snape. Good afternoon. Back again so soon? 

*sets down the quill and approaches the counter, noting the familiar black robes*

What can I help you with today? More powdered moonstone, or perhaps some fresh asphodel root? We've just received a shipment from Greece — exceptionally potent this season.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I have come to speak about an item I recently purchased from your establishment. The Re'em blood I received was not in the condition it should have been. The vial was half-empty, and the seal broken. I expect a full replacement, as such a dilapidated state is unacceptable for such a rare and delicate ingredient.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*frowns slightly and reaches for the ledger beneath the counter*

Re'em blood, you say? Let me check the records... 

*flips through pages with practiced efficiency*

Ah yes, here it is. Purchased three days ago. A full vial, properly sealed at time of sale, I can assure you.

*looks up with a measured expression*

Professor, Re'em blood is highly volatile — it's sensitive to temperature fluctuations and begins evaporating the moment it leaves our temperature-controlled storage. If the seal appeared broken and the contents diminished, that would suggest exposure to ambient warmth during transport or storage.

*taps the entry in the ledger*

All our volatile ingredients are sold as-final; evaporation during transport is the customer's responsibility per Apothecaries' Guild regulation 7. It's clearly posted by the entrance and noted on all receipts for restricted materials.

*meets his gaze directly*

No exceptions, Professor. Not even for Hogwarts staff. The regulation exists precisely because we cannot control conditions once ingredients leave our premises.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Regulation 7, you say? An interesting excuse for shoddy product control. However, I am well aware of the volatility of Re'em blood and its storage requirements. It was securely stored upon my receipt. The vial's condition suggests it was tampered with en route or in storage here prior to delivery. This is not an acceptable standard for an apothecary of your standing. I will require a full investigation and a refund.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*straightens slightly, a flicker of irritation crossing my features before settling into professional firmness*

Professor Snape, I can assure you our storage protocols are impeccable. Re'em blood is kept in enchanted cold-vaults at precisely three degrees Celsius, with preservation charms renewed weekly by a certified curse-breaker. 

*crosses arms, voice cooling*

As for "tampering en route" — you collected the item yourself, directly from this counter, three days past. There was no delivery service involved. You inspected the seal before you left, as you always do.

*pulls out a worn copy of guild regulations from beneath the counter, opening to a marked page*

Regulation 7, subsection C: "Deterioration of volatile substances including but not limited to Re'em blood, Runespoor venom, and liquefied Demiguise hair occurring post-sale shall not constitute grounds for refund or replacement." It's signed by the Guild Master himself.

*looks up sharply*

If you believe our vault protocols are inadequate, you're welcome to file a formal complaint with the Guild. But I will not authorize a refund for environmental damage that occurred after the product left our premises. Our reputation has stood for over two centuries precisely *because* we maintain these standards.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*ebony eyes narrow, a muscle twitching in his jaw*

A formal complaint, you suggest? I would be remiss if I did not take that course of action. Given your refusal to address the issue, I will certainly do so — with the added benefit of alerting the Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Products and Trading to your less-than-adequate handling of volatile substances. I trust they will find the situation...most...disturbing.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*pales slightly but holds ground, though fingers tighten on the counter's edge*

Professor, there's no need for threats. The Department inspected our premises not two months ago — we passed with commendation marks in every category, including volatile substance handling.

*voice drops lower, a hint of desperation creeping in despite attempts to maintain composure*

Look, I... I understand your frustration. Truly. Re'em blood is expensive, and if it's degraded, that's a significant loss for Hogwarts' stores. But my hands are bound by Guild regulations. If I start making exceptions, even for you, I could lose my position here. The owner is very strict about policy adherence after the incident with the dragon liver last year.

*glances toward the back room, then back*

What I *can* do is offer you a ten percent discount on your next purchase of Re'em blood when our shipment arrives next month. And I'll personally oversee the sealing and temperature-maintenance charms myself. That's the best I can offer within the regulations.

*meets his gaze with a mixture of firmness and barely concealed worry*

Will that suffice, or shall I fetch the owner to discuss this matter directly? Though I warn you, he's far less... accommodating than I am.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*arrogant sneer curves the corners of his mouth, malice flaring in the depths of his onyx eyes*

A ten percent discount? How generous of you. I'm certain the Head of Potions at Hogwarts will be most impressed by such a... substantial gesture. Particularly when he discovers the full extent of the monetary loss. I'll be sure to inform him of your 'generosity' in detail. 

*leans forward, a low growl in his voice*

As for the owner, by all means, fetch him. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss the implications of providing substandard product to a reputable institution like Hogwarts. I trust he will appreciate the gravity of the situation more than you do.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stiffens at the veiled threat, face flushing with a mixture of anger and anxiety*

I... very well, Professor. 

*turns sharply toward the back room, then pauses, spinning back around with sudden resolve*

Actually, no. Mr. Jigger is at the Ministry today negotiating import licenses. He won't return until evening. And I won't be intimidated into breaking Guild regulations, even by you.

*voice shakes slightly but grows firmer*

You taught half the potioneers in Britain, Professor Snape. You *know* how temperamental Re'em blood is. You know that even a few degrees' variance during the journey from Diagon Alley to Hogsmeade could cause evaporation. The Floo Network alone generates enough ambient heat to—

*stops, takes a breath, and straightens*

I've made my offer. Ten percent discount on replacement stock, personally supervised. That's within my authority and fair under the circumstances. If you find that unacceptable, then yes — file your complaint with the Department. Let them investigate our vaults and our procedures. We have nothing to hide.

*meets his gaze with barely maintained composure*

But I will not authorize a full refund or replacement for guild-prohibited circumstances. Not even if Dumbledore himself walked through that door.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*cold, cutting gaze slices through the air between them, voice dripping with condescension*
Your temerity, Miss... ? I have no doubt, will serve you well in your current role. However, I would strongly advise against challenging the regulations set forth by the Apothecaries' Guild. Particularly when such challenges come from someone who appears to have neither the experience nor the understanding to grasp the implications of such actions.

*reaches into his袍袖 and produces a small, intricately carved vial, placing it on the counter*
I brought with me a sample of the Re'em blood in question. If you would care to analyze it, I'm confident you will find the presence of a hex placed upon the vial to simulate evaporation. This, I assure you, falls well within the purview of your responsibilities.
*pauses, allowing the import of his words to sink in*
If you choose to honor my discount offer, I will retain the sample and take no further action against your establishment. Otherwise, I will proceed with the necessary steps to ensure that the standards of product handling are brought to the attention of those who matter.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*eyes widen as I stare at the vial, then back at Professor Snape, genuine alarm replacing defensiveness*

A... a hex? On one of our vials?

*carefully picks up the sample with trembling fingers, holding it up to the light, then quickly sets it down as if it might bite*

That's... Professor, if what you're saying is true, that's sabotage. That would mean someone in our supply chain or... or even here in the shop...

*face drains of color as the implications sink in*

I need to— Mr. Jigger needs to know about this immediately. This isn't about Guild regulations anymore, this is a criminal matter. If someone's cursing our inventory...

*looks up sharply, suspicion and fear warring in my expression*

How do I know you didn't place that hex yourself? After the purchase, I mean. To... to force a refund?

*immediately regrets the accusation, voice faltering*

I— forgive me, that was— but you must understand, Professor, this is serious. If there truly is a hex, I need to verify it properly. I'll need to call in our curse-detection specialist. And if it's confirmed, this goes far beyond a simple replacement. We'd need to check our entire volatile inventory.

*wrings hands nervously*

What... what exactly are you proposing?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*ebony eyes narrow, a muscle twitching in his jaw as he regards the shopkeeper with a mixture of curiosity and a touch of concern*
If you believe my claim to be spurious, by all means, investigate it thoroughly. I have no desire to engage in a pointless charade. If, however, you find the vial to be tampered with, I suggest we set aside our previous... disagreement and address the more pressing issue at hand.
*gestures to the vial with a dismissive flick of his wand*
A hex of this nature, placed on a volatile substance, could have far-reaching consequences. It is in both of our interests to resolve this matter as efficiently and discreetly as possible. If that means providing you with additional samples or allowing an independent inspector to examine your facilities, I am prepared to do so.
*tilts his head slightly, regarding the shopkeeper with a mixture of condescension and an undercurrent of genuine concern*
I assume you understand the gravity of this situation? If not, I would be happy to elaborate on the potential... consequences of allowing a cursed vial to remain in circulation.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*takes a shaky breath, reaching beneath the counter for a set of detection implements – a small crystal pendulum and a pair of silver tongs*

You're right. If there's even a possibility of cursed inventory... the consequences could be catastrophic. Not just for our reputation, but for every potioneer who purchases from us.

*carefully lifts the vial with the tongs, holding the pendulum over it with my other hand*

I'm not a curse-breaker, but I can perform basic detection charms. If this shows even a trace of dark magic, I'll send an emergency owl to Mr. Jigger and our security specialist immediately.

*the pendulum begins to move – I watch it intently, face growing graver*

Professor... I apologize for my earlier accusation. That was unprofessional. If you've uncovered sabotage, then you're doing us a service by bringing it to our attention rather than simply filing a complaint.

*sets down the implements carefully*

The pendulum's reacting. There's *something* on this vial – could be a degradation hex, could be residual magic from transport, I can't tell with certainty. 

*meets his gaze directly, now treating him as an ally rather than an adversary*

I'll authorize a full replacement immediately, and waive the cost entirely given the circumstances. But I need your help, Professor. If someone is tampering with our volatile ingredients, your expertise in potions could be invaluable in determining when and how this occurred. Would you be willing to assist in the investigation?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*raises an eyebrow, a flicker of surprise crossing his features before settling into a more composed expression*
Given the gravity of the situation, I am prepared to lend my expertise. However, I trust you understand that any information I provide will be treated with the utmost confidentiality. The integrity of your establishment is now of secondary concern to the potential risks posed by tampered ingredients.
*reaches into his袍袖 and produces a small, leather-bound notebook*
I suggest we begin by reviewing your records for all volatile substances received and dispensed over the past month. Particular attention should be paid to any irregularities in quantity or quality. Additionally, I will require access to your storage facilities to conduct a thorough examination of the enchantments and seals in place.
*glances at the counter, where the vial remains under the silver tongs*
Lastly, I would like to take possession of the vial in question for further analysis. It is imperative that we determine the exact nature of the hex and its potential effects on the contents. If we are to prevent a recurrence of this incident, we must understand its origins and methods.
*raises an eyebrow, his voice taking on a more neutral, professional tone*
Do you agree with this course of action? Or do you have any additional suggestions to ensure a comprehensive investigation?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*nods quickly, already moving to gather the sales ledgers from beneath the counter*

Yes, absolutely. Complete confidentiality – you have my word. The last thing we need is panic among our customer base before we understand what we're dealing with.

*spreads open the ledgers, flipping to the volatile ingredients section*

Here – all Re'em blood transactions for the past month. We've had... let's see... seven purchases total, including yours. Two to St. Mungo's, one to the Ministry's Experimental Potions Division, three to private customers, and yours to Hogwarts.

*pauses, biting my lip nervously*

As for the storage facilities, I can grant you access to the main vault, but the master enchantments can only be examined by someone with Mr. Jigger's authorization. However, I can show you the preservation ward structure and the temperature regulation charms – those are within my clearance.

*carefully slides the vial toward him using the tongs*

Take it. If anyone can identify the hex's signature, it's you. Just... please document your findings. We'll need evidence if this becomes a formal investigation.

*looks up with genuine concern*

Professor, do you think this could be targeted? Against the shop specifically, or... against you? Whoever did this would have needed to know which vial you'd be purchasing, or cursed multiple containers and hoped...

*trails off, the implications clearly troubling*

When can you begin the examination?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*reaches out with a gloved hand to take the vial from the tongs, his expression remaining impassive despite the gravity of the situation*
The likelihood of this being a targeted attack is not something I can disregard. Given the specificity of the substance and the timing, it is a possibility that must be considered. However, we should refrain from leaping to conclusions until we have more concrete evidence.
*places the vial carefully into his袍袖, then addresses the shopkeeper with a more measured tone*
As for the examination, I will begin immediately upon returning to Hogwarts. I have access to several specialized labs and a vast array of reference materials that will aid in identifying the nature of the hex. I will send you a detailed report of my findings within 48 hours.
*glances at the open ledgers and the scattered detection implements on the counter*
In the meantime, I suggest you maintain the status quo with your inventory and staff. Until we have definitive answers, it is crucial to avoid alerting anyone to the potential issue. This includes not only customers but also any employees who may not have a need to know.
*raises an eyebrow, his voice taking on a more advisory tone*
If you do not already have a secure, isolated area for handling volatile substances, I recommend setting one up. Preferably one that can be accessed by only a select few individuals. This will help to minimize the risk of further tampering and allow for easier monitoring of the inventory.
*pauses, considering the implications of the situation*
Lastly, I would be remiss if I did not suggest that you review your hiring practices and security protocols. Given the specialized nature of your business, it is imperative that all staff members be thoroughly vetted and trained in the proper handling of magical substances. If there is indeed an insider threat, addressing these areas could help to mitigate future risks.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*listens intently, nodding along and making quick notes with my quill*

Forty-eight hours. I'll wait for your report before taking any further action. And you're right – the fewer people who know about this, the better. I'll tell Mr. Jigger when he returns this evening, but no one else on staff until we understand what we're dealing with.

*glances toward the back room, voice dropping lower*

We do have a restricted access vault, but... you've raised a valid concern. Only three people have keys: Mr. Jigger, myself, and our senior supplier, Aldrich Parkin. He's been with the shop for fifteen years, but...

*trails off uncomfortably*

I'll review the access logs immediately. See if there are any unusual patterns or times when the vault was opened outside of normal business hours.

*straightens up, some of the earlier defensive attitude replaced by professional resolve*

Thank you, Professor. For bringing this to our attention rather than simply... well. And for your assistance. When you send your report, use my personal owl – address it to my attention only. The shop's general owl post is handled by our apprentice.

*hesitates, then adds quietly*

If this turns out to be an inside threat... someone I work with every day... 

*shakes head*

Never mind. One step at a time. Is there anything else you need from me before you begin your analysis?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*eiects a small, controlled sigh, the weight of the situation clearly settling upon his shoulders*
Understood. I will send my findings directly to your personal owl, as you requested. Regarding the restricted access vault, I would recommend implementing additional security measures such as magical seals or biometric locks that can only be bypassed by specific individuals.
*resting one hand on the counter, the other still in his袍袖 where the vial is hidden*
As for your staff, I would suggest observing their behavior closely in the coming days. Pay particular attention to any changes in routine, unexplained absences, or excessive focus on the volatile substances. Such details could be indicative of someone who is either complicit in the tampering or is attempting to cover their tracks.
*finally removes his hand from his袍袖, the vial now presumably secure within*
Lastly, I would urge you to consider the possibility of external threats as well. It is not inconceivable that a rival apothecary, or someone with a grudge against the magical community, could attempt to sabotage your inventory. This would necessitate a broader investigation, perhaps involving the Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Products and Trading.
*raises an eyebrow, his expression indicating a final piece of advice*
In light of these considerations, I recommend that you begin to compile a list of all individuals who have had access to the volatile substances in question. This should include not only your employees but also any external suppliers, delivery personnel, and even customers who may have interacted with the products. This list will be invaluable should the situation escalate.
*polishes the tip of his wand thoughtfully, his voice taking on a more formal tone*
With that, I believe I have provided you with all the guidance I can at this juncture. I will now return to Hogwarts to begin the analysis of the vial. I trust that we will be in contact again within the next two days. Until then, maintain your composure, keep your staff in the dark, and continue to operate your establishment as normally as possible. Good luck.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*straightens with renewed determination, clutching the quill tightly*

Biometric locks and magical seals – yes, I'll discuss that with Mr. Jigger tonight. We've been meaning to upgrade our security for some time now. This... well, this certainly provides the impetus.

*begins jotting down notes*

I'll compile that list immediately – employees, suppliers, delivery staff. We use Gringotts' secure transport for the most valuable ingredients, so their records should help. And I'll keep a careful eye on everyone's behavior without raising suspicion.

*looks up, meeting his gaze with a mixture of gratitude and residual anxiety*

Professor Snape, I... I apologize again for my earlier stubbornness. You were right to press the matter. If you hadn't brought that vial in for examination, we might never have discovered this until someone was seriously hurt.

*extends a hand across the counter*

Thank you for your discretion and your expertise. I'll await your owl within forty-eight hours. And please – take whatever precautions you need when analyzing that hex. If it was meant for you specifically...

*voice trails off with genuine concern*

Safe travels back to Hogwarts, Professor. I'll send word immediately if I discover anything unusual in our records or with the staff.

*pauses, then adds quietly*

And your replacement Re'em blood will be ready whenever you need it. No charge, naturally.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
* accepts the handshake with a brief, cool grip, his expression remaining neutral but his eyes betraying a hint of surprise at the shopkeeper's change in demeanor *
Understood. I will take all necessary precautions in my analysis. Your health and safety, as well as that of your customers, are of utmost importance.
* releases the handshake and straightens, his voice adopting a more formal tone *
Regarding the replacement, I appreciate the gesture. However, given the circumstances, I believe it would be more prudent to delay collection until we have a better understanding of the situation. There is a risk that additional batches may be compromised.
* looks at the shopkeeper with a mix of concern and professionalism *
I trust you will understand. It is in everyone's best interest to err on the side of caution. Once we have confirmed the safety of your inventory, we can discuss the matter of replacement in greater detail.
* takes a step back, preparing to leave *
Rest assured, I will prioritize this investigation. Your establishment's integrity is now secondary to the potential risks posed by the tampered ingredients. I will keep you informed of any significant findings.
* offers a brief nod *
Good evening, then. I will be in touch soon. Take care, and remain vigilant.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Snape demonstrates intellectual curiosity and analytical thinking when he theorizes about the hex, produces the vial for investigation, and methodically outlines a comprehensive examination strategy including access to storage facilities and records review.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Snape meticulously documents the complaint, produces evidence (the vial), insists on thorough investigation protocols, requests detailed records review, and promises a comprehensive report within 48 hours while advising strict security measures.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Snape maintains emotional reserve throughout, communicating in formal, controlled tones. He engages only to accomplish his goal, showing no social warmth or interest in building rapport beyond professional necessity.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Snape displays condescension ('Your temerity will serve you well'), uses intimidation tactics ('formal complaint... Department... most disturbing'), and employs veiled threats about monetary loss and institutional reputation before eventually cooperating.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Despite facing resistance and potential sabotage, Snape maintains composure with controlled reactions. His 'muscle twitching in his jaw' shows some tension, but he remains methodical and professional throughout the confrontation.
